A1.justification: Despite the changed title and substantially expanded scope, v2 retains identifiable theory and experiments from v1. Both complete PDFs, including their equations, figures and appendices, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original trained-network experiments measuring permutation accuracy and required ensemble size.

after.justification: Appendix E retains the original trained-network experiments. Appendix B also reports numerical validation of permutation, addition and multiplication using the NTK predictor.

M1.justification: v1 learns fixed permutations from standard basis vectors. v2 introduces blockwise algorithmic templates, orthonormal input encoding, iterative state updates with rounding, and auxiliary zero-label training templates for multiplication and SBN. These substantially extend the procedure while retaining the two-layer ReLU network and ensemble principle.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only binary permutations. v2 adds numerical evaluation of binary addition and multiplication, including iterative algorithm execution, while retaining permutation experiments. SBN is supported by a theoretical construction, without reported empirical evaluation.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing learning methods. The empirical/numerical versus theoretical curves concern the proposed approach itself. Methods such as Neural GPU and NALU added to v2's related work are not experimental comparators.

E3.justification: The retained permutation experiments still use width 50,000, 1,000 test vectors with two nonzero entries, and the same accuracy measures. New validation computes the NTK predictor and applies encoding and rounding through algorithm execution for bit lengths up to 10. Figure 5 separately calculates ensemble requirements accounting for all inputs and execution steps.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained permutation ensemble-size studies, Figure 5 adds numerical scaling diagnostics for the variance-to-squared-mean ratio underlying the ensemble bound. Neither version reports component ablations or distribution-shift tests.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Independent ensemble members remain part of the method; the expanded Gaussian variance and concentration analysis concerns theoretical guarantees rather than new empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v1's Figure 1 curves are retained as v2's Figure 7. New Figure 5 reports numerical and theoretical ensemble-complexity curves for permutation, addition and multiplication, with matching growth rates up to constants. Appendix B additionally reports correct NTK-predictor execution through 10-bit inputs. These are added results, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds formal template-matching definitions, Assumption 5.1 controlling unwanted correlations, a generalized predictor theorem, and constructive arithmetic/SBN proofs. It extends ensemble analysis to O(k'b + k' log m) across inputs and iterations. The new Theorem 5.1 statement also reverses the sign convention used in its own proof.

C1.justification: v1 claims exact permutation learning with logarithmic training size and quadratic ensemble complexity. v2 claims exact learnability of algorithmic instructions covering addition, multiplication and SBN, extending to computable functions through SBN. Algorithmic template representation becomes a central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 develops the decision-margin and unwanted-correlation explanation for composing local computations. Section 7 explicitly identifies orthogonal training examples and access to primitive instructions as restrictions. Appendix E additionally explains that computational requirements prevented trained-network experiments on addition and multiplication.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C add detailed block layouts, instruction specifications, initial states, bit encodings, iteration counts and auxiliary training examples. v2 names Neural Tangents for numerical validation and describes a demonstration script. Its code pointer changes from permlearn to binary_algos; the retained permutation experiment's principal settings remain documented.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially reoriented toward algorithm learning and arithmetic, adding discussion of Neural GPU, NALU/NAU/NMU, scratchpads, positional encodings and chain-of-thought methods. Much of v1's universal-approximation, domain-adaptation and double-descent discussion is removed, and the contribution is positioned around exact algorithmic learnability.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten. The main text is reorganized around template execution and a two-part learnability argument; detailed derivations and the original training experiments are placed in appendices. The conclusion becomes a focused limitations and future-work section.

P2.justification: v2 adds framework, addition, encoding and predictor diagrams, a three-panel complexity figure with insets, and an SBN schematic. Extensive boxed instruction displays and pseudocode also change the presentation. The original paired experimental figure is retained and relocated to Appendix E as Figure 7.

improvement.justification: v2 adds a reusable framework, detailed constructions, arithmetic validation and clearer limitations. However, Theorem 5.1 states the opposite sign mapping to its proof, and Appendix B.4 computes M[a] - M[b] whereas Algorithm 1 specifies M[b] - M[a]. The reported numerical validation does not cover SBN. These unresolved inconsistencies affect the expanded guarantees, preventing a reliable judgment that the substantial additions yield a net overall quality improvement.
